people.descriptor: Official and Father of Guo Wei
Military Commissioner and Imperial Heir Designate
Empress and Mother of Guo Wei

value.cause: killed when Liu Rengong seized Shunzhou

units.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝，姓郭氏，邢州堯山人也。
units.en: Taizu, temple name the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, Martial, Filial Emperor, was of the Guo clan and came from Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
units.literal: Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, Martial, Filial Emperor—surname Guo, a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

units.zh: 父簡，事晉為順州刺史。
units.en: His father Jian had served the Jin as prefect of Shunzhou.
units.literal: His father Jian served Jin as prefect of Shunzhou.

units.zh: 劉仁恭攻破順州，簡見殺，子威少孤，依潞州人常氏。
units.en: When Liu Rengong seized Shunzhou, Jian was killed. Wei was still a boy and, orphaned, was taken in by the Chang family of Luzhou.
units.literal: Liu Rengong took Shunzhou; Jian was killed. Young son Wei was left alone and relied on the Chang clan of Luzhou.

units.zh: 潞州留後李繼韜募勇敢士為軍卒，威年十八，以勇力應募。
units.en: Li Jitao, regent of Luzhou, was raising bold men for the ranks; at eighteen Wei enlisted on the strength of his daring.
units.literal: Luzhou regent Li Jitao recruited brave men as soldiers; at eighteen Wei volunteered for his courage and strength.

units.zh: 為人負氣，好使酒，繼韜特奇之。
units.en: Proud-spirited and quick to drink, he caught Jitao’s eye as someone out of the ordinary.
units.literal: By nature proud and bold, he was fond of drink; Jitao regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 威嘗遊於市，市有屠者，常以勇服其市人。
units.en: Wei once walked the market where a butcher ruled the stalls by sheer bravado.
units.literal: Once when Wei was strolling in the market, there was a butcher who by his boldness cowed the market folk.

units.zh: 威醉，呼屠者，使進幾割肉，割不如法，叱之。
units.en: Drunk, Wei hailed the butcher for a few slices; the cuts displeased him and he shouted the man down.
units.literal: Wei, drunk, called the butcher to bring cuts of meat; when the cutting was not to his liking, he berated him.

units.zh: 屠者披其腹示之曰：「爾勇者，能殺我乎？」
units.en: The butcher ripped open his robe and cried, “You’re the brave one—dare you kill me?”
units.literal: The butcher bared his belly and said, “You are the brave one—can you kill me?”

units.zh: 威即前取刀刺殺之。
units.en: Wei strode up, seized the knife, and ran him through.
units.literal: Wei stepped forward, took the knife, and stabbed him to death.

units.zh: 一市皆驚，威頗自如。
units.en: The market erupted in alarm; Wei himself was unruffled.
units.literal: The whole market was shocked; Wei was quite composed.

units.zh: 為吏所執，繼韜惜其勇，陰縱之使亡，已而復召置麾下。
units.en: The authorities arrested him, but Jitao valued his daring and quietly set him loose; before long he called him back into his service.
units.literal: Officers seized him; Jitao prized his courage and secretly let him flee, then later recalled him to his command.

units.zh: 繼韜叛晉附於梁，後莊宗滅梁，繼韜誅死，其麾下兵悉隸從馬直，威以通書算補為軍吏。
units.en: When Jitao turned on Jin for Liang, Zhuangzong later crushed Liang and put Jitao to death. The remnant force entered the Imperial Horse Guard, and Wei, skilled in letters and accounts, was posted as a clerk.
units.literal: Jitao rebelled against Jin and joined Liang; later Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and Jitao was executed. His troops were all assigned to the Imperial Horse Guard; for knowing writing and reckoning Wei was made a clerical officer.

units.zh: 好讀《閫外春秋》，略知兵法，後為侍衛軍吏。
units.en: He read the Spring and Autumn Outside the Gate and picked up a rough grasp of warfare; he later served as a clerk in the Palace Guard.
units.literal: He liked to read the Spring and Autumn Outside the Gate and had some knowledge of military strategy; later he became a clerk in the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 漢高祖為侍衛親軍都虞候，尤親愛之。
units.en: Han Gaozu, then chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, took a particular liking to him.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu was chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, he was especially fond of Wei.

units.zh: 後高祖所臨鎮，嘗以威從。
units.en: Afterward, on every posting Gaozu held, Wei usually went along.
units.literal: Later, wherever Gaozu garrisoned, he often brought Wei with him.

units.zh: 契丹滅晉，漢高祖起兵太原，即皇帝位，拜威樞密副使。
units.en: After the Khitan overthrew Jin, Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan and claimed the throne, naming Wei Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
units.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan and took the throne, appointing Wei Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

units.zh: 乾祐元年正月，高祖疾大漸，以隱帝托威及史弘肇等。
units.en: In the first month of Qianyou 1, as Gaozu lay dying, he committed the Hidden Emperor to the care of Wei, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest.
units.literal: In the first month of Qianyou 1, Gaozu’s illness grew grave; he entrusted the Hidden Emperor to Wei, Shi Hongzhao, and others.

units.zh: 隱帝即位，拜威樞密使。
units.en: On the Hidden Emperor’s accession, Wei became Commissioner of the Privy Council.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor acceded, Wei was made Commissioner of the Privy Council.

units.zh: 是歲三月，河中李守貞、永興趙思綰、鳳翔王景崇相次反，隱帝遣白文珂、郭從義、常思等分討之，久皆無功。
units.en: In the third month of that year Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Zhao Sixian at Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang rose one after another. The Hidden Emperor dispatched Bai Wenke, Guo Congyi, Chang Si, and others on separate campaigns, yet month after month they could not break the rebels.
units.literal: That year in the third month, Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang rebelled in succession. The Hidden Emperor sent Bai Wenke, Guo Congyi, Chang Si, and others to suppress them separately; for a long time none achieved success.

units.zh: 隱帝謂威曰：「吾欲煩公可乎？」
units.en: The Hidden Emperor asked Wei, “May I burden you with this command?”
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor said to Wei, “I wish to trouble you—would that be acceptable?”

units.zh: 威對曰：「臣不敢請，亦不敢辭，惟陛下命。」
units.en: Wei answered, “I would not presume to request it, nor dare I decline—only obey Your Majesty.”
units.literal: Wei replied, “Your servant dares not ask for it, yet dares not refuse—only Your Majesty’s order.”

units.zh: 乃加拜威同中書門下平章事，使西督諸將。
units.en: He was made Associate Grand Councilor and sent west to take command of the armies.
units.literal: He was then promoted to Associate Grand Councilor and sent west to oversee the generals.

units.zh: 威居軍中，延見賓客，褒衣博帶，及臨陣行營，幅巾短後，與士卒無異；
units.en: In camp he met guests in formal robes and wide belt; on the march or at the front he wore a kerchief and short jacket like any soldier—
units.literal: In camp Wei received guests in full court dress with broad sash; when he went to battle or inspected the lines he wore a headcloth and short coat at the rear, no different from the rank and file;

units.zh: 上所賜予，與諸將會射，恣其所取，其餘悉以分賜士卒，將士皆歡樂。
units.en: imperial gifts he laid out at target practice for the commanders to claim at will, and whatever remained went to the troops. The army was elated.
units.literal: what the throne bestowed he shared at archery with the officers, letting them take what they wished; the rest he gave outright to the men, and officers and soldiers alike rejoiced.

units.zh: 威至河中，自柵其城東，思柵其南，文珂柵其西，調五縣丁二萬人築連壘以護三柵。
units.en: At Hezhong Wei walled the east, Chang Si the south, and Bai Wenke the west, while twenty thousand laborers from five counties threw up connecting works to guard the three siegelines.
units.literal: When Wei reached Hezhong he fortified east of the city himself; Si fortified the south and Wenke the west, and levies from five counties—twenty thousand men—built linked ramparts to shield the three camps.

units.zh: 諸將皆謂守貞窮寇，破在旦夕，不宜勞人如此，威不聽。
units.en: His officers insisted Shouzhen was spent and would collapse any day, and that so much conscription was wasteful. Wei paid them no heed.
units.literal: The generals all said Shouzhen was a cornered foe and would fall within days, and that such labor on the people was needless; Wei would not listen.

units.zh: 已而守貞數出兵擊壞連壘，威輒補之，守貞輒復出擊，每出必有亡失。
units.en: Shouzhen soon began raiding the lines again and again; Wei patched each breach, and every attack left the rebels weaker.
units.literal: Before long Shouzhen repeatedly sallied to smash the linked works; Wei repaired them each time, and every sortie cost Shouzhen losses.

units.zh: 久之，城中兵食俱盡，威曰：「可矣！」
units.en: When provisions inside the walls ran out, Wei declared, “Now we may strike!”
units.literal: After long months, food and fodder inside the city were exhausted. Wei said, “It is time!”

units.zh: 乃治攻具，為期日，四面攻之，破其羅城，守貞與妻子自焚死，思綰、景崇相次降。
units.en: He readied assault machines, fixed the assault for a set day, and stormed from every quarter until the outer wall fell. Shouzhen perished with his family in the flames; Sixian and Jingchong submitted one after the other.
units.literal: He prepared siege engines, set a day, and attacked on four sides; they breached the outer wall. Shouzhen burned himself with wife and children; Sixian and Jingchong surrendered in turn.

units.zh: 隱帝勞威以玉帶，加檢校太師兼侍中，威辭曰：「臣事先帝，見功臣多矣，未嘗以玉帶賜之。」
units.en: The Hidden Emperor honored Wei with a jade belt and made him Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant. Wei refused: “Under the late emperor I watched countless men of merit, and none were given a jade belt.”
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor rewarded Wei with a jade belt and added Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant. Wei declined, saying, “When I served the late emperor I saw many meritorious ministers, yet never saw a jade belt bestowed.”

units.zh: 因言：「臣幸得率行伍，假漢威靈以破賊者，豈特臣之功，皆將相之賢，有以安朝廷，撫內外，而饋餉以時，故臣得以專事征伐。」
units.en: He added, “I have only led common soldiers and, under Han’s authority, crushed the rebels—that triumph is not mine alone. The court’s wise ministers kept the realm calm and the convoys punctual; only then could I fight without distraction.”
units.literal: He went on, “Your servant was fortunate to lead the ranks and, borrowing Han’s majesty, break the rebels—this is not merit mine alone. It is the worth of the chief ministers who steadied the court within and without and sent supplies on time, so that I could devote myself to the campaign.”

units.zh: 隱帝以威為賢，於是悉召楊邠、史弘肇、蘇逢吉、禹珪、竇貞固、王章等皆賜以玉帶，威乃受。
units.en: Moved, the Hidden Emperor called in Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Su Fengji, Yu Gui, Dou Zhengu, Wang Zhang, and the others and belted them too; then Wei accepted his own.
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor, deeming Wei worthy, then summoned Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Su Fengji, Yu Gui, Dou Zhengu, Wang Zhang, and the rest and gave them jade belts as well; only then did Wei accept.

units.zh: 威又推功大臣，請加爵賞，於是加貞固司空，逢吉司徒，禹珪、邠左右僕射。
units.en: Wei pressed the case for his fellow ministers, and Dou Zhengu was elevated to Minister of Works, Su Fengji to Minister of Education, Yu Gui and Yang Bin to Vice Directors of the Left and Right.
units.literal: Wei again pushed merit on the great ministers and asked that ranks and rewards be raised; thereupon Dou Zhengu was made Minister of Works, Su Fengji Minister of Education, and Yu Gui and Yang Bin Vice Directors of the Left and Right.

units.zh: 已而又曰：「此特漢廷親近之臣耳。
units.en: He said further, “That covers only the Han court’s inner circle.
units.literal: He then said, “These are only Han’s intimates at court.

units.zh: 漢諸宗室、天下方鎮，外暨荊、浙、湖南，皆未及也。」
units.en: The imperial house of Han, every frontier command, and even Jing, Zhe, and Hunan in the south still go unrewarded.”
units.literal: Han’s imperial clansmen, the military commissioners throughout the realm, and even Jing, Zhe, and Hunan in the south have not yet been included.”

units.zh: 由是濫賞遍於天下。
units.en: Rewards then spilled across the empire without measure.
units.literal: Thus indiscriminate rewards spread across the empire.

units.zh: 是冬，契丹寇邊，威以樞密使北伐，至魏州，契丹遁。
units.en: That winter, with Khitan raids on the frontier, Wei led a northern campaign as Privy Commissioner. At Weizhou the invaders melted away.
units.literal: That winter, when the Khitan raided the border, Wei marched north as Privy Commissioner; he reached Weizhou and the Khitan withdrew.

units.zh: 三年二月，師還。
units.en: In the second month of year three the troops came home.
units.literal: In the second month of the third year the army returned.

units.zh: 四月，拜威鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使，仍以樞密使之鎮。
units.en: In the fourth month he was named regent of Yedu and military commissioner of Tianxiong, retaining the Privy Council and going out to the command.
units.literal: In the fourth month Wei was made regent of Yedu and military commissioner of Tianxiong, still holding the Privy Council post while governing the command.

units.zh: 宰相蘇逢吉以謂樞密使不可以藩鎮兼領，與史弘肇等固爭。
units.en: Chancellor Su Fengji argued that the Privy Commissioner must not double as a military commissioner; he and Shi Hongzhao fought the appointment to the end.
units.literal: Chancellor Su Fengji held that the Privy Commissioner could not also hold a frontier command, and he and Shi Hongzhao stubbornly opposed it.

units.zh: 久之，卒以樞密使行，詔河北諸州皆聽威節度。
units.en: At last Wei departed as Privy Commissioner, with an edict placing all Hebei prefectures under his authority.
units.literal: After long dispute, Wei finally went as Privy Commissioner; an edict ordered every prefecture in Hebei to obey his command.

units.zh: 隱帝與李業等謀，已殺史弘肇等，詔鎮寧軍節度使李弘義殺侍衛步軍指揮使王殷於澶州，又詔侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇殺威及宣徽使王峻於魏。
units.en: The Hidden Emperor and Li Ye had already struck down Shi Hongzhao and his allies. He now ordered Li Hongyi of Zhenning to murder Wang Yin, foot commander of the Palace Guard, at Chanzhou, and Guo Chong, horse commander, to kill Wei and Wang Jun, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, at Wei prefecture.
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor plotted with Li Ye and others; having already killed Shi Hongzhao and his faction, he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Palace Guard foot commander Wang Yin at Chanzou, and cavalry commander Guo Chong to kill Wei and Palace Secretariat commissioner Wang Jun at Wei.

units.zh: 詔書先至澶州，弘義恐事不果，反以詔書示殷，殷與弘義遣人告威。
units.en: The Chanzou order arrived first. Li Hongyi, afraid the scheme would miscarry, showed the edict to Wang Yin; Yin and Hongyi dispatched a messenger to alert Wei.
units.literal: The edict reached Chanzou first; Hongyi feared the plot would fail and instead showed the edict to Wang Yin; Yin and Hongyi sent a man to warn Wei.

units.zh: 已而詔殺威、峻使者亦馳騎至，威匿詔書，召樞密使院吏魏仁浦謀於臥內。
units.en: Then came the courier charged with executing Wei and Jun. Wei concealed the edict and called Privy Council clerk Wei Renpu to his bedside for counsel.
units.literal: Soon the messenger bearing orders to kill Wei and Jun galloped up as well. Wei hid the edict and summoned Privy Council clerk Wei Renpu to counsel him in his bedchamber.

units.zh: 仁浦勸威反，教威倒用留守印，更為詔書，詔威誅諸將校以激怒之，將校皆憤然效用。
units.en: Renpu urged revolt and showed him how to reverse the regent’s seal and issue a counterfeit order for Wei to kill his commanders. The officers, furious, rallied to him as one.
units.literal: Renpu urged rebellion and taught Wei to misuse the regent’s seal and forge a new edict ordering Wei to execute his officers—thereby enraging them, and every officer angrily pledged his service.

units.zh: 十一月丁丑，威遂舉兵渡河。
units.en: On dingchou in the eleventh month Wei marched and crossed the Yellow River.
units.literal: On dingchou of the eleventh month Wei raised troops and crossed the river.

units.zh: 隱帝遣開封尹侯益、保大軍節度使張彥超、客省使閻晉卿等率兵拒威，又遣內養瑽脫覘威所向。
units.en: The Hidden Emperor dispatched Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, Zhang Yanchao of Baoda, Yan Jinqing of the guest-reception office, and others to meet Wei in battle, and sent the palace attendant Zongtuo to track his march.
units.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent Kaifeng governor Hou Yi, Baoda army commissioner Zhang Yanchao, guest-reception commissioner Yan Jinqing, and others with troops to block Wei, and also sent palace attendant Zongtuo to spy on his movements.

units.zh: 瑽脫為威所得，威乃附脫奏請縛李業等送軍中。
units.en: Zongtuo fell into Wei’s hands, and Wei used him to forward a memorial demanding Li Ye and his party be bound and delivered to camp.
units.literal: Zongtuo was captured; Wei had him attach a memorial asking that Li Ye and the others be bound and sent to the army.

units.zh: 隱帝得威奏，以示業等，業等皆言威反狀已白，乃悉誅威家屬於京師。
units.en: The Hidden Emperor read the memorial to Li Ye’s circle; they declared Wei’s guilt proven and put every member of his household in the capital to death.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor received Wei’s memorial and showed it to Li Ye and the others, they said Wei’s treason was already clear, and they executed all of Wei’s family in the capital.

units.zh: 庚辰，威至滑州，義成軍節度使宋延渥叛於漢來降。
units.en: On gengchen Wei entered Huazhou; Song Yanwo of Yicheng broke with Han and came over.
units.literal: On gengchen Wei reached Huazhou; Yicheng military commissioner Song Yanwo rebelled against Han and surrendered.

units.zh: 壬午，犯封丘。
units.en: On renwu he attacked Fengqiu.
units.literal: On renwu he assaulted Fengqiu.

units.zh: 甲辰，及泰寧軍節度使慕容彥超戰於劉子陂，彥超敗，奔於兗州。
units.en: On jiachen he met Murong Yanchao of Taining at Liuzipo, routed him, and drove him toward Yanzhou.
units.literal: On jiachen he fought Taining military commissioner Murong Yanchao at Liuzipo; Yanchao was defeated and fled to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 郭允明反，弒隱帝於趙村。
units.en: Guo Yunming turned traitor and murdered the Hidden Emperor at Zhao Village.
units.literal: Guo Yunming rebelled and assassinated the Hidden Emperor at Zhao Village.

units.zh: 丙戌，威入京師，縱火大掠。
units.en: On bingxu Wei entered the capital; fires blazed and the troops looted freely.
units.literal: On bingxu Wei entered the capital, set fires, and allowed plunder.

units.zh: 戊子，率百官朝太后於明德門，請立嗣君。
units.en: On wuzi he led the civil and military officials to the Bright Virtue Gate to bow before the Empress Dowager and beg that a successor be chosen.
units.literal: On wuzi he led the hundred officials to the Bright Virtue Gate to greet the Empress Dowager and ask that a successor be enthroned.

units.zh: 太后下令：文武百寮、六軍將校，議擇賢明，以承大統。
units.en: The Empress Dowager commanded the court and the six armies to choose a worthy man to bear the succession.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager issued an order: civil and military officials and commanders of the six armies were to deliberate and select a worthy man to receive the great mandate.

units.zh: 庚寅，威率百官詣明德門，請立武寧軍節度使赟為嗣。
units.en: On gengyin Wei brought the ministers again to the Bright Virtue Gate and proposed Liu Yun, military commissioner of Wuning, as heir.
units.literal: On gengyin Wei led the officials to the Bright Virtue Gate and asked that Wuning military commissioner Yun be made heir.

units.zh: 遣太師馮道迎赟於徐州。
units.en: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao was sent to fetch Yun from Xuzhou.
units.literal: He sent Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome Yun from Xuzhou.

units.zh: 辛卯，請太后臨朝聽政，以王峻為樞密使，翰林學士、尚書兵部侍郎範質為副使。
units.en: On xinmao he had the Empress Dowager preside at court. Wang Jun became Privy Commissioner; Fan Zhi, Hanlin academician and Minister of War, vice commissioner.
units.literal: On xinmao he asked the Empress Dowager to hold court; Wang Jun was made Privy Commissioner, and Hanlin academician and Minister of War Fan Zhi became vice commissioner.

units.zh: 十二月甲午朔，威北伐契丹，軍於滑州。
units.en: On jiawu, the new moon of the twelfth month, Wei marched north against the Khitan and stopped at Huazhou.
units.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, jiawu, Wei campaigned north against the Khitan and halted at Huazhou.

units.zh: 癸丑，至澶州而旋。
units.en: On guichou he came to Chanzou and wheeled about.
units.literal: On guichou he reached Chanzou and turned back.

units.zh: 王峻遣郭崇以騎七百逆劉赟於宋州，殺之，其將鞏廷美、楊溫為赟守徐州。
units.en: Wang Jun dispatched Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to cut off Liu Yun at Songzhou and kill him. Yun’s officers Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen still defended Xuzhou in his name.
units.literal: Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horse to intercept Liu Yun at Songzhou and kill him; his generals Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen held Xuzhou for Yun.

units.zh: 戊午，次臯門，漢宰相竇貞固、蘇禹珪來勸進。
units.en: On wuwu he camped at Gao Gate, where Han chancellors Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui came to press him to ascend.
units.literal: On wuwu he stopped at Gao Gate; Han chancellors Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui came to urge him to take the throne.

units.zh: 庚申，太后制以威監國。
units.en: On gengshen the Empress Dowager named Wei regent of the realm.
units.literal: On gengshen the Empress Dowager issued an order making Wei regent.

units.zh: 廣順元年春正月丁卯，皇帝即位，大赦，改元，國號周。
units.en: On dingmao in the first month of Guangshun 1 the emperor was enthroned, proclaimed a general amnesty, and declared the dynasty Zhou.
units.literal: In the first month of Guangshun 1, spring, on dingmao, the emperor took the throne, granted a great amnesty, changed the era name, and the state was called Zhou.

units.zh: 己巳，上漢太后尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
units.en: On jisi he honored the Han empress dowager as Illustrious Sage Empress Dowager.
units.literal: On jisi he gave the Han Empress Dowager the honorific title Illustrious Sage Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 戊寅，漢劉崇自立於太原。
units.en: On wuyin Liu Chong of the northern Han regime proclaimed himself emperor at Taiyuan.
units.literal: On wuyin Liu Chong of Han declared himself emperor at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 吳、蜀諸國自立，皆絕而不書，此書，與其不屈于周，語在十國年譜論。
units.en: Wu, Shu, and the other states that set themselves up were all excluded from the record. This case is written in approval of Liu Chong’s refusal to submit to Zhou; the explanation appears in the discussion to the Chronological Tables of the Ten Kingdoms.
units.literal: When Wu, Shu, and the other states established themselves, they were all cut off and not recorded. This one is recorded in approval of his not yielding to Zhou; the explanation is in the discussion in the Chronological Tables of the Ten Kingdoms.

units.zh: 己卯，馮道為中書令。
units.en: On jimao Feng Dao was made Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: On jimao Feng Dao became Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 二月辛丑，西州回鶻使都督來。
units.en: On xinchou in the second month envoys came from the Western Xizhou Uighurs.
units.literal: On xinchou in the second month, an envoy from the Western Xizhou Uighurs arrived.

units.zh: 丁未，契丹兀欲遣使裊骨支來。
units.en: On dingwei Wuyu of the Khitan sent the envoy Liaoguzhi.
units.literal: On dingwei the Khitan Wuyu sent the envoy Liaoguzhi.

units.zh: 癸丑，寒食，望祭於蒲池。
units.en: On guichou, the Cold Food Festival, he performed a distant-offering sacrifice at Puchi Pool.
units.literal: On guichou, Cold Food Festival, he offered distant sacrifice at Puchi Pool.

units.zh: 丁巳，尚書左丞田敏使於契丹。
units.en: On dingsi Tian Min, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was dispatched to the Khitan.
units.literal: On dingsi Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Min was sent as envoy to the Khitan.

units.zh: 回鶻使摩尼來。
units.en: The Uighur envoy Mani arrived.
units.literal: The Uighur envoy Mani arrived.

units.zh: 三月甲戌，武寧軍節度使王彥超克徐州。
units.en: On jiaxu in the third month Wang Yanchao of Wuning took Xuzhou.
units.literal: On jiaxu in the third month, Wuning military commissioner Wang Yanchao captured Xuzhou.

units.zh: 鞏廷美、楊溫不書死之，語在贇傳。
units.en: Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen are not recorded as “dying for it”; the explanation appears in Yun’s biography.
units.literal: Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen are not written as having died for it; the explanation is in Yun’s biography.

units.zh: 夏四月甲午，立夫人董氏為德妃。
units.en: On jiawu in the fourth month Lady Dong was made Virtuous Consort.
units.literal: On jiawu in the fourth month of summer, Lady Dong was established Virtuous Consort.

units.zh: 五月辛未，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：高祖璟謚曰睿和，廟號信祖，祖妣張氏謚曰睿恭；
units.en: On xinwei in the fifth month he posthumously honored his ancestors as emperors and ancestresses as empresses: great-great-grandfather Jing, posthumous title Ruihe, temple name Xinzu; great-great-grandmother Lady Zhang, posthumous title Ruigong;
units.literal: On xinwei in the fifth month he posthumously honored ancestors as emperors and ancestresses as empresses: great-grandfather Jing, posthumous title Ruihe, temple name Xinzu; great-grandmother Lady Zhang, posthumous title Ruigong;

units.zh: 曾祖諶謚曰明憲，廟號僖祖，祖妣申氏謚曰明孝；
units.en: great-grandfather Chen, posthumous title Mingxian, temple name Xizu; great-grandmother Lady Shen, posthumous title Mingxiao;
units.literal: great-great-grandfather Chen, posthumous title Mingxian, temple name Xizu; great-great-grandmother Lady Shen, posthumous title Mingxiao;

units.zh: 祖蘊謚曰翼順，廟號義祖，祖妣韓氏謚曰翼敬；
units.en: grandfather Yun as emperor Yishun, temple Yizu, and grandmother Lady Han as empress Yijing;
units.literal: grandfather Yun, posthumous title Yishun, temple name Yizu; grandmother Lady Han, posthumous title Yijing;

units.zh: 考謚曰章肅，廟號慶祖，妣王氏謚曰章德。
units.en: father Jian as emperor Zhangsu, temple Qingzu, and mother Lady Wang as empress Zhangde.
units.literal: father, posthumous title Zhangsu, temple name Qingzu; mother Lady Wang, posthumous title Zhangde.

units.zh: 六月辛亥，範質及戶部侍郎判三司李穀為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: On xinhai Fan Zhi and Li Gu, Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of the Three Bureaus, were made Vice Directors and Associate Grand Councilors.
units.literal: On xinhai Fan Zhi and Li Gu, Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Three Bureaus, became Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.

units.zh: 竇貞固、蘇禹珪罷。
units.en: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui left office.
units.literal: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui were dismissed.

units.zh: 癸丑，範質參知樞密院事。
units.en: On guichou Fan Zhi was added to the Privy Council.
units.literal: On guichou Fan Zhi joined in managing Privy Council affairs.

units.zh: 丁巳，宣徽北院使翟光鄴為樞密副使。
units.en: On dingsi Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, became Vice Privy Commissioner.
units.literal: On dingsi Northern Bureau Palace Secretariat commissioner Zhai Guangye became Vice Privy Commissioner.

units.zh: 秋七月戊寅，幸王峻第。
units.en: On wuyin in the seventh month the emperor called at Wang Jun’s home.
units.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on wuyin the emperor visited Wang Jun’s residence.

units.zh: 八月壬寅，契丹來歸趙瑩之喪。
units.en: On renyin in the eighth month the Khitan sent back Zhao Ying’s remains.
units.literal: On renyin in the eighth month the Khitan returned the coffin of Zhao Ying.

units.zh: 冬十月丙午，漢人來討，討加有罪，漢之於周，義所得誅。
units.en: On bingwu of winter’s tenth month, Han came on a punitive campaign. “Punish” is used for applying penalty to the guilty; in relation to Zhou, Han had the moral claim to execute them.
units.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu, the Han people came to punish. “Punish” means imposing punishment on guilt; as between Han and Zhou, Han had the righteous ground to execute them.

units.zh: 攻自晉州。
units.en: The attack came from Jinzhou.
units.literal: They attacked from Jin Prefecture.

units.zh: 云「自晉州」者，見漢兵當誅罪人于京師，自晉州而入耳。
units.en: The phrase “from Jinzhou” shows that Han’s troops should have punished the guilty at the capital itself, and that Jinzhou was only their route of entry.
units.literal: It says “from Jin Prefecture” to show that the Han troops ought to have executed the guilty men at the capital, and merely entered from Jin Prefecture.

units.zh: 攻城無得失不書，此書者，許漢來討。
units.en: An attack on a city is normally omitted if nothing is gained or lost; this one is written because the text recognizes Han’s punitive claim.
units.literal: When an attack on a city has no gain or loss, it is not recorded; this is recorded because the text approves Han’s coming to punish.

units.zh: 十一月，王峻及建雄軍節度使王彥超拒之。
units.en: In the eleventh month Wang Jun and Wang Yanchao of Jianxiong met them in the field.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Wang Jun and Jianxiong military commissioner Wang Yanchao resisted them.

units.zh: 十二月，慕容彥超反。
units.en: In the twelfth month Murong Yanchao rose in revolt.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Murong Yanchao rebelled.

units.zh: 二年春正月甲子，侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英為兗州行營都部署。
units.en: On jiazi in the first month of year two, Cao Ying, foot commander of the Palace Guard, was named overall commander of the Yanzhou campaign.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, on jiazi, Palace Guard foot commander Cao Ying was made overall deployment commissioner for the Yanzhou field headquarters.

units.zh: 庚午，高麗王昭使其廣評侍郎徐逢來。
units.en: On gengwu King Zhao of Goryeo sent Xu Feng, vice director of broad appraisal.
units.literal: On gengwu King Zhao of Goryeo sent his Broad Appraisal Vice Director Xu Feng.

units.zh: 二月庚寅，府州防禦使折德扆克岢嵐軍。
units.en: On gengyin in the second month Zhe Dewei of Fuzhou took Kelan garrison.
units.literal: On gengyin in the second month, Fuzhou defense commissioner Zhe Dewei captured Kelan garrison.

units.zh: 三月丁巳朔，寒食，望祭於郊。
units.en: On dingsi, the new moon of the third month and the Cold Food Festival, he sacrificed at the suburban altars.
units.literal: On the first day of the third month, dingsi, Cold Food Festival, distant sacrifice at the suburbs.

units.zh: 戊辰，內客省使鄭仁誨為樞密副使，翟光鄴罷。
units.en: On wuchen Zheng Renhui of the palace guest office became Vice Privy Commissioner, and Zhai Guangye was removed.
units.literal: On wuchen palace guest commissioner Zheng Renhui was made Vice Privy Commissioner; Zhai Guangye was dismissed.

units.zh: 夏五月庚申，東征，李穀留守東都，鄭仁誨為大內都點檢。
units.en: On gengshen in the fifth month the emperor marched east. Li Gu stayed as regent at Luoyang; Zheng Renhui was named chief inspector of the inner palace.
units.literal: On gengshen in the fifth month of summer the eastern campaign: Li Gu remained regent at the eastern capital, and Zheng Renhui was overall inspector of the inner palace.

units.zh: 癸亥，次曹州，赦流罪以下囚。
units.en: On guihai he paused at Caozhou and freed all convicts short of exile.
units.literal: On guihai he halted at Caozhou and pardoned prisoners below exile.

units.zh: 乙亥，克兗州。
units.en: On yihai Yanzhou fell.
units.literal: On yihai Yanzhou was taken.

units.zh: 彥超投井死，故不書伏誅。
units.en: Yanchao died by throwing himself into a well, so the text does not say he “was executed.”
units.literal: Yanchao threw himself into a well and died, so the text does not write that he was executed.

units.zh: 壬午，赦兗州。
units.en: On renwu Yanzhou received an amnesty.
units.literal: On renwu Yanzhou was granted amnesty.

units.zh: 六月乙酉朔，幸曲阜，祠孔子。
units.en: On yiyou, the new moon of the sixth month, he went to Qufu and offered sacrifice to Confucius.
units.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, yiyou, he visited Qufu and sacrificed to Confucius.

units.zh: 庚子，至自兗州。
units.en: On gengzi he came back from Yanzhou.
units.literal: On gengzi he returned from Yanzhou.

units.zh: 秋九月乙丑，太僕少卿王演使於高麗。
units.en: On yichou in the ninth month Wang Yan, vice director of the Palace Stud, was sent to Goryeo.
units.literal: On yichou in the ninth month of autumn, Palace Stud Vice Director Wang Yan was sent as envoy to Goryeo.

units.zh: 契丹寇邊。
units.en: The Khitans raided the border.
units.literal: The Khitans raided the frontier.

units.zh: 三年春正月乙卯，麟州刺史楊重訓叛於漢，來附。
units.en: In the first month of spring in year 3, on yimao day, Lin Prefecture governor Yang Chongxun rebelled against Later Han and defected to Zhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, on the day yimao, Yang Chongxun, military governor of Lin Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.

units.zh: 閏月丙戌，回鶻使獨呈相溫來。
units.en: In the intercalary month, on bingxu day, the Uyghur envoy Duxing Xiangwen arrived.
units.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day bingxu, the Uyghur envoy Duxing Xiangwen came.

units.zh: 二月甲子，貶王峻為商州司馬。
units.en: In the second month, on jiazi day, Wang Jun was demoted to military adjutant of Shang Prefecture.
units.literal: In the second month, on the day jiazi, Wang Jun was demoted to military adjutant of Shang Prefecture.

units.zh: 三月甲申，封榮為晉王。
units.en: In the third month, on jiashen day, Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
units.literal: In the third month, on the day jiashen, Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 不書子者，榮於禮不得為子，不書子則當書其本姓，又不書者，周人所共諱。
units.en: The text does not call Rong a son because ritually he could not be one. If it avoided “son,” it should have given his original surname, but it omits that too because the people of Zhou collectively tabooed it.
units.literal: It does not write “son” because according to ritual Rong could not be a son; if it did not write “son,” it ought to write his original surname, but that too is not written because it was what the Zhou people all avoided saying.

units.zh: 丙戌，鄭仁誨罷。
units.en: On bingxu day, Zheng Renhui was dismissed from office.
units.literal: On the day bingxu, Zheng Renhui was dismissed.

units.zh: 己丑，棣州團練使王仁鎬為左衛大將軍、樞密副使。
units.en: On jichou day, Di Prefecture training commissioner Wang Renhao became Grand General of the Left Guard and deputy military affairs commissioner.
units.literal: On the day jichou, Wang Renhao, training commissioner of Di Prefecture, was made Grand General of the Left Guard and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 夏六月，大雨，水。
units.en: In the sixth month of summer, heavy rains brought flooding.
units.literal: In summer, the sixth month, great rain fell and there was flooding.

units.zh: 秋七月，契丹盧臺軍使張藏英來奔。
units.en: In the seventh month of autumn, Khitan Lutai army commissioner Zhang Cangying defected to Zhou.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Cangying, army commissioner of the Khitan Lutai command, came in flight to submit.

units.zh: 九月，吐渾党富達等來。
units.en: In the ninth month, Tuyuhun Dang Fuda and others arrived.
units.literal: In the ninth month, Tuyuhun Dang Fuda and others came.

units.zh: 冬十月庚申，馮道為奉迎神主使。
units.en: In the tenth month of winter, on gengshen day, Feng Dao was appointed commissioner to welcome the ancestral tablets.
units.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengshen, Feng Dao was made commissioner to welcome the ancestral tablets.

units.zh: 十一月癸未，党項使吳帖磨五等來。
units.en: In the eleventh month, on guimao day, Tangut envoy Wu Tiemo and a party of five arrived.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day guimao, the Tangut envoy Wu Tiemo and others of the fifth rank came.

units.zh: 十二月戊申，四廟神主至自西京，迎之於西郊，祔於太廟。
units.en: In the twelfth month, on wushen day, spirit tablets from the four temples arrived from the Western Capital. They were received at the western suburb and installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wushen, the spirit tablets of the four temples arrived from the Western Capital; they were met at the western suburb and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 壬申，殺天雄軍節度使王殷。
units.en: On renshen day, Tianxiong army governor Wang Yin was executed.
units.literal: On the day renshen, Wang Yin, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was executed.

units.zh: 乙亥，享於太廟。
units.en: On yihai day, the emperor offered sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: On the day yihai, offerings were presented in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 顯德元年春正月丙子朔，有事於南郊，大赦，改元，群臣上尊號曰聖明文武仁德皇帝。
units.en: On the new-year day bingzi in the first month of spring, Xiande 1, the southern suburb rites were performed. A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name changed, and the ministers honored him as Sagely, Bright, Martial, Civil, Benevolent, and Virtuous Emperor.
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Xiande, on the first day of the month, bingzi, the southern suburb rites were performed, a general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed, and the ministers elevated the honorific title to Sagely, Bright, Martial, Civil, Benevolent, and Virtuous Emperor.

units.zh: 戊寅，罷鄴都。
units.en: On wuyin day, the Ye capital district was abolished.
units.literal: On the day wuyin, Ye Capital was abolished.

units.zh: 丙戌，鎮寧軍節度使鄭仁誨為樞密使。
units.en: On bingxu day, Zhenning army governor Zheng Renhui was made military affairs commissioner.
units.literal: On the day bingxu, Zheng Renhui, military governor of the Zhenning army, was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 壬辰，端明殿學士、戶部侍郎王溥為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，王仁鎬罷。
units.en: On renchen day, Duanming Hall academician and vice minister of revenue Wang Pu became vice director of the Secretariat and associate chancellor; Wang Renhao was dismissed.
units.literal: On the day renchen, Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue, was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery; Wang Renhao was dismissed.

units.zh: 是日，皇帝崩於滋德殿。
units.en: That same day the emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue.
units.literal: On that day the emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue.

units.zh: 年五十一。
units.en: He was fifty-one.
units.literal: He was fifty-one years old.
